Primitives

Stat glyph

A printed stat: the game's own mark, with the value the card prints beside it. docs/DESIGN.md asked for "cost in a hexagonal plate, power and defence in chamfered plates at the corners" and the component drew exactly that for several phases. It renders LSS's published symbols now, and the note below says what changed and what the plates are still for.

0cost
3power
2defence
20life
4intellect
1arcane

The symbol sits outboard and the numeral inboard of it, which is how the card sets its combat bar: {p} 4 at one end and 2 {d} at the other, with the artwork against the frame in both corners. On the card panel the end corner mirrors, so the marks line the two edges and the numerals face in toward the type line between them. Cost is the one exception — the card sets that numeral inside the resource disc, and so does this.

Nothing on the card panel is labelled. The words above are the gallery naming what it is showing you; the product prints none, because the card prints none and the marks are the ones a reader has already met. What the label used to carry lives in the accessible name, which spells the stat out in full — "Power 3", "No printed power" — at every size.

A stat the card does not print — which is not a stat printed 0.

0cost
cost
0power
power
0defence
defence

1,648 cards print a cost of 0, 191 a defence of 0 and 13 a power of 0, so both members of each pair above are real and a reader has to be able to tell them apart. The mark survives the absence — it is what says WHICH stat is missing — and it greys out rather than disappearing, with no character at all in the value position. An en dash sat there until the values moved out of the plates; beside a mark, where every printed value now is, a dash reads as something the card prints. Spoken as "no printed power", which is where a claim about what is not on a card belongs.

This is the one thing the drawn plates did better. An absence used to be a recessed fill — a token, in the theme, checked like every other colour. An ingested PNG takes no token, so the greyed state is a filter instead. That is the price of rendering the game's own file, and it is stated here rather than discovered.

The card page draws these three whether or not a card fills them, because the frame reserves the positions; a hero, which has none of them, gets none.

The plates are the fallback, and they are still here. The component draws them wherever no artwork is supplied — in a story, where the site's public/ is not mounted, and for the one stat the rules print no symbol for. The house vocabulary is a square plate, chamfered differently, and none of them is eight-sided: the pitch jewel owns that outline and the system promises it means pitch.

One size, three areas, so the boxes are not all the same. The eye compares ink rather than bounding boxes: a chamfered plate keeps about 21% more of its box than a disc does. Each plate is therefore scaled by the square root of its silhouette's area against the disc's π/4. Four of the six are discs and so take the reference factor untouched — only the shield and arcane's chamfered plate are compensated, which is what makes the row above read as one size. The marks do not need it: the files are all square and all full-bleed, so the artwork resets the factor to one.

Arcane is the exception, and it is the one that proves the rule. 1.12.4 names eight symbols and arcane is not among them, so LSS publishes no icon for it and there is no printed register to take. It is the only stat that meets the plate in the product — and the card panel never asks for it at all, because the card prints that number in its rules text instead.

The plates reproduce no LSS symbol: they are the system's own shapes carrying our numerals, every colour a token. The marks above them are LSS's files, unmodified, ingested from LSS's own rules site with the provenance record docs/COMPLIANCE.md §3 requires. §3 bars logos and close semblances of them and blesses drawing from a mechanic; {p} is defined at 1.12.4d as the notation for a power value and identifies no brand. Cost is the one place a numeral is set over the artwork rather than beside it — the file is unaltered, the numeral is a separate element, and the composite is ours.
